raw_response:
Ai, let me think about this year's plan. I'll say it the way I think it, then we can sort it out proper.

---

Well, I'm 73 now. Fifty years on this dirt, same village, same wells. My old woman and me, we can still do the light work, but the heavy stuff — plowing, harvest — my second son comes back from the factory for a few days, or we pay the machine man. Thirteen mu ain't a lot but it keeps rice in the pot.

I split the land the way I always have. The sandier patch on the west, about 4 mu, that's cotton — cotton does alright on that soil and wheat don't do so well there. The other 9 mu and a bit, that's wheat then maize, wheat then maize, been that way twenty years. Don't need to change what works.

**Wheat** — I put it in back in October, same as always. Went in around the 10th after the Cold Dew. Used the seed from Old Wang's shop, the Jimai variety the neighbors all use — didn't save my own, hasn't been worth it since the good varieties came out. Before planting I put down about one bag of compound (that diammonium, the 15-15-15) per mu, that's 50 jin, mixed in with the plow. Now it's April, the wheat is greening up and starting to joint — I'll topdress with urea, maybe half a bag per mu, 20 jin or so, when the ground is wet from irrigation. I already watered once after winter, gonna water again at jointing and one more at the grain-filling stage if it don't rain. Three waters, maybe four if May is dry. Pumping costs — that meter runs fast, so I don't waste it. Last year I got about 400 kg off a mu, year before was 380. I'm hoping for 400 again, you can't count on more than you got before.

Pests — I'll spray once for the weeds around green-up, that 2,4-D stuff the agro shop sells. Aphids sometimes come at the head stage, if I see 'em I spray, if not I don't bother.

**Maize** — right after wheat harvest in June, no time to waste, the ground is still warm and the combine man comes through on Monday and the planter comes Wednesday, that's how tight it is. I buy the hybrid seed, the Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has that year, costs near 60 yuan a mu but you can't skimp on maize seed, you plant the cheap stuff and the ears come out small. Put down compound at planting, about 40 jin per mu, and then when the maize is waist-high and the big bell stage comes, I topdress with urea, maybe 25 jin per mu. That's what my neighbor Lao Zhang does and his maize always looks good. Water once or twice if July-August is dry. Last year maize gave me about 450 kg/mu, year before was better, about 480, but it rained more that year.

Herbicide before the maize comes up — I always do that, else the pigweed takes over. One spray for corn borer at tasseling if I see the damage.

**Cotton** — the 4 mu on the west. This is the hard one, lot of work, and prices ain't what they were when I was young. But I know cotton. Plant end of April when the soil warms up, use the hybrid seed from the co-op, maybe 80-90 yuan a mu. Cotton don't want too much nitrogen, you get all leaf no boll — so about 40 jin urea total per mu, split, some at planting and more at flowering. Phosphorus and potassium at planting. Irrigate twice usually, once at budding and once at flowering if the summer is dry.

The thing with cotton is the spraying. Bollworm, aphids, spider mites — I spray maybe 5-6 times through the summer, whatever the agro shop man tells me is the pest that week. That costs money but you skip a spray and you lose half the bolls. Picking starts in September, three-four rounds through October. My old woman and me pick what we can, and when it's heavy I pay two village women 80 yuan a day each for a week.

Cotton yield — I'm hoping 220 jin lint per mu. Used to do better when I was younger but my back ain't what it was.

**The money side** — I figure this year I'll spend around 7,000-7,500 yuan on inputs all told, and that's already tight. I don't have cash to put down more fertilizer even if they say it would help. Last year I spent about that and it worked out. If the wheat price is low at harvest I might hold some back and sell in winter when it comes up.
